panels.title: Scrape up
panels.description: 1 = Prometheus scraped /metrics. It does not prove the engine is stepping; see Wedge.

panels.title: Wedge
panels.description: 1 when requests are queued or running but the engine has not completed a step in the last minute: a hung kernel keeps /metrics alive while generation is dead (the vLLM cuDNN FP8 hang).

panels.title: Tokens per second (aggregate)
panels.description: Counters advance when a request finishes, so rates are smoothed over request length. Prompt = all prompt tokens; the cached series is the part served from the reused KV prefix (no prefill work).

panels.title: Decode speed (tok/s per stream)
panels.description: Tokens after the first divided by decode time, over finished requests: rate(itl_count) / rate(itl_sum). Per-stream speed, so it does not grow with batch size.

panels.title: Prefill speed (tok/s, uncached prompt)
panels.description: Uncached prompt tokens divided by time-to-first-token over finished requests: (rate(prompt) - rate(cached)) / rate(ttft_sum). TTFT also contains the first sampled token and, with --max-batch, the wait behind other prefill chunks, so this is a lower bound on raw prefill speed.

panels.title: Engine steps per second
panels.description: One step is a prefill chunk or a decode step. Flat zero while requests are running means a wedge.

panels.title: Inter-token latency
panels.description: Per-request mean ITL, weighted by token count.

panels.title: TTFT distribution
panels.description: Requests finishing per TTFT bucket (heatmap of intarsia_ttft_seconds). Buckets reach 300 s for long contexts.

panels.title: ITL distribution
panels.description: Requests finishing per inter-token-latency bucket (token-weighted per-request mean).

panels.title: Prompt tokens per request (percentiles)
panels.description: Per-request prompt length, includes tokens served from the KV prefix cache.

panels.title: Generated tokens per request (percentiles)
panels.description: Per-request completion length.

panels.title: Generation length distribution
panels.description: Requests per generated-length bucket.

panels.title: Finished requests per second by reason
Error ratio
panels.description: Share of finished requests that ended with reason=error, plus 429 rejections per second on the right axis series. Client cancellations are not errors.

panels.title: Rejected (HTTP 429) per second
panels.description: Queue-full refusals (server --max-queue and engine queue). Non-zero means clients are being turned away.

panels.title: Request rate by client
panels.description: Requests admitted per second by client. The label comes from the X-Intarsia-Client request header, else the User-Agent product token; at most 16 values, the rest are 'other'.

panels.title: Tokens per second by client
panels.description: Tokens of finished requests per second by client and kind.

panels.title: Batch queue depth
panels.description: Requests accepted by the batch scheduler and not yet holding a KV slot (batch engine only, --max-batch N). Empty on CUDA and HIP: those backends run one sequence at a time, so there is no batch scheduler to report.

panels.title: Average decode batch size
panels.description: Approximation: generated tokens per second divided by batched decode passes per second (one token per row per pass; speculative decoding raises it). Counters move when requests finish, so it lags a little. Empty on CUDA and HIP: those backends run one sequence at a time, so there is no batch scheduler to report.

panels.title: Decode passes by batch size
panels.description: Batched decode passes per second, stacked by the number of rows in the pass. Empty on CUDA and HIP: those backends run one sequence at a time, so there is no batch scheduler to report.

panels.title: Scheduler iteration time
panels.description: Wall time of a scheduler iteration that ran a decode step (histogram, batch engine). Empty on CUDA and HIP: those backends run one sequence at a time, so there is no batch scheduler to report.

panels.title: Batch TTFT (submit to first token)
panels.description: Includes queue wait, unlike intarsia_ttft_seconds. Empty on CUDA and HIP: those backends run one sequence at a time, so there is no batch scheduler to report.

panels.title: Prefill chunks and mixed iterations
panels.description: Prefill chunks per second, and iterations that ran a prefill chunk right after a decode phase (decoding requests waited behind the chunk). Empty on CUDA and HIP: those backends run one sequence at a time, so there is no batch scheduler to report.

panels.title: Scheduler request outcomes per second
panels.description: admitted, finished, cancelled, failed, rejected (batch engine). Empty on CUDA and HIP: those backends run one sequence at a time, so there is no batch scheduler to report.

panels.title: Device memory
panels.description: On unified-memory machines (GB10, Apple) this is shared with the OS and other services.

panels.title: Kernel time share
panels.description: Share of sampled launch time per op over the selected rate window. GPU backends time one launch in N (profile_every), so shares are statistical.

panels.title: Op time rate
panels.description: Sampled seconds of op time per second of wall time.
